score.note: Fifth pass: re-checked the panel's previously-rejected 'two independent velocity accumulators' experiment now that the r4-trampoline fix shifted the whole function's register-pressure landscape, per this pass's own instruction. On the new baseline it is a real, substantial win rather than the regression it was before: changed the inner loop's velocity update from a single accumulator (velocity_b = -velocity_a recomputed fresh every iteration) to two independent accumulators at the loop bottom (`velocity_b -= outer << 3; velocity_a += outer << 3;`, in that statement order -- the reverse order scored one wrong_instruction worse). Effect: `work` now lands in fp, matching the reference, for the first time since the r4-fix landed -- confirmed via --align: `mov fp, r2`, `add r5, fp`, `mov r1, fp`, and the stack frame size (sub sp,#52) are all byte-identical to reference now. star->r6, j->r7, and velocity_b->r8 also now match exactly. differing_halfwords 278->272, wrong_instructions 185->155 (a 30-instruction drop, the strongest evidence yet this whole line of fixes is real). Traced the actual REG_ALLOC_ORDER in alchemy-gcc/agscc/gcc/config/arm/arm.h ({r3,r2,r1,r0,ip,lr,r4,r5,r6,r7,r8,sl,r9,fp,sp,pc,...}) to characterize the one remaining register mismatch precisely: candidate puts velocity_a->sl, outer->r9; reference has them reversed. Tried ~8 targeted reshapes to flip this specific swap (M2C_FIELD/draw_destination read order, local declaration order, hoisting velocity_a/velocity_b init earlier, an explicit neg_outer variable mirroring the reference's spilled -outer, an explicit named step variable, deriving velocity_a from velocity_b instead of vice versa, reversing the outer>quarter comparison operand order, reshaping the (j>=0?j:j+3)>>2 ternary into an explicit if) -- every one either had zero effect or regressed (one badly, evicting work from fp again). All remaining diff regions (an interleaved-vs-duplicated scheduling difference in the star decay block, an extra branch+duplicate shift in both quarter-ternary computations, and pop{r0} vs pop{r1} in the epilogue) trace back to this same sl/r9 swap rather than being independently fixable. Confirms this register choice is genuinely sensitive to something not yet identified, not a fixed rule -- not pursued further per the ban on forcing register assignment. Still not exact. Fourth pass's note below (renamed) remains otherwise accurate.
score.prior_note_2026_08_27d: Fourth pass: resolved the family's cross-owner 'Func_080072f4 5th-argument-in-r4' mystery, which every prior pass (this owner and all three siblings) had flagged as a genuinely unprecedented, unresolvable ABI quirk. It is not an ABI quirk. games/gs1/asm/080072e4.s (kind runtime_thunk_bundle) is fourteen `call_via_rN` trampolines (`bx rN; mov r8,r8`, 4 bytes each) at 0x080072e4+4*N for N=r0..sp; 0x080072f4 is exactly the r4 entry (4th slot: r0,r1,r2,r3,r4 -> 0x080072e4,e8,ec,f0,f4). `bl Func_080072f4` in the retained assembly is `bl <call_via_r4>`, an INDIRECT call through whatever function pointer is in r4 at the call, not a direct call to a real 7-argument function. Confirmed definitively three ways: (1) `arm_function_arg` in alchemy-gcc/agscc/gcc/config/arm/arm.c returns NULL_RTX (stack) once 4 registers are used, with zero special-case logic for a 5th register argument -- this compiler's own source proves it can never place ANY argument in r4; (2) tracing the value loaded into r4 right before the call back to its origin shows it comes from `add r1, sp, #20; bl Func_080cef64` earlier in the function -- exactly sp+20, the address passed as `out_pair` to Func_080cef64, i.e. r4 holds callback_pair[0], the draw-callback function pointer, not a plain argument; (3) the already-adopted games/gs1/src/battle/effects/member_orbit/run.c (main:080ce85c) already models this exact pattern correctly as `((DrawRectangleFn)rectangle_slot[slot & 1])(canvas, src, x, y, 32, 32)` -- a cast-and-call through a function-pointer array slot, not a call to a symbol named Func_080072f4 at all. Rewrote this owner's call the same way: `((DrawRectangleFn) callback_pair[0])(draw_destination, (void*)(src_off+(s32)work), y, h, raw, raw<<1)`, a 6-argument indirect call matching DrawRectangleFn's real signature, and removed the fictional `void Func_080072f4(s32,s32,s32,s32,DrawRectangleFn,s32,s32)` prototype entirely. Verified structurally against games/gs1/asm/080dc1ec.s via --align: the candidate now reproduces the reference's exact 'stage w/h to stack, reload dest+callback from earlier stack slots into r0/r4, bl <trampoline>' instruction pattern at the call site, byte-for-byte in shape (only the absolute stack offsets differ, tracking an overall frame-size difference). Also fixed a second, smaller finding surfaced by --align once the call was correct: `Func_080e0524(140, work, 1, 1)` -- the reference loads 140 from the literal pool (`ldr r0,[pc,...]`), not a `movs` immediate, matching the established Value_XXXXXXXX idiom; changed to `Func_080e0524((s32)&Value_0000008c, work, 1, 1)`. Net effect of both fixes: wrong_instructions dropped sharply (235->185, the strongest evidence this is a real correctness gain) while differing_halfwords rose slightly (245->278) and candidate_bytes shrank (612->592) -- the same 'small metric regression traded for real correctness' pattern already validated repeatedly this session (see prior_note_2026_08_27b), not a reason to revert. matched_prefix also dropped (12->7), confirming register allocation is globally sensitive to this fix the same way the dispatch-shape lever proved earlier -- the panel's three merged wins (dispatch-shape/clamp-locals/array-locals) may partially or fully re-apply differently now that the call site is modeled correctly; a follow-up pass should re-attempt them against this new baseline before assuming they still hold. The dominant remaining divergence is now the already-documented work-register choice (candidate keeps work in r9, reference in fp, diverging from the very first `mov`/`ldmia` sequence) -- unchanged by this pass, deliberately not chased further here. This finding applies to all three siblings (080e01e4, 080d82b0, 080d59b0) that share the identical fictional Func_080072f4 call pattern; fixed there too in the same session pass, see their own dossiers.
score.prior_note_2026_08_27c: Third pass: a 4-way diverse-lever panel (four isolated worktree agents, each attacking a different, non-overlapping section of the function) ran against the 277-dh/270-wi baseline from prior_note_2026_08_27b. Two levers were pure no-ops on differing_halfwords (a setup-section reshape, and extracting `j & 3` into a named local under the switch); two produced real, independently-verified improvements, and both merged cleanly since they touch disjoint code: (1) dispatch-shape -- rewriting the `switch (j & 3)` 4-way dispatch as an if-else chain shaped to match the reference's own compare tree (`selector > 1` first, splitting into the {2,3} and {0,1} groups) changed register-allocation decisions across the WHOLE function, not just locally, dropping differing_halfwords 277->246; (2) clamp-locals -- `half = (raw + ((u32) raw >> 31)) >> 1` was compiling to a logical `lsrs` instead of the reference's arithmetic `asrs`, because `(u32) raw >> 31` promotes the whole sum to unsigned under the usual arithmetic conversions even though the result is stored into an s32; casting back to `(s32) ((u32) raw >> 31)` before the addition restored the signed sum and the asrs, though on its own this only changed wrong_instructions (270->268), not differing_halfwords. A third, independently-tried lever (array-locals: recomputing `star = (u8*)0x02010000 + j*28` inside the loop instead of resetting once and incrementing by 28 each iteration) scored 276/252 alone and also merged cleanly. All three combined: differing_halfwords 245, wrong_instructions 235 (down from 277/270) -- the merge is strictly additive, better than any single lever. Still not exact. The panel's dispatch-shape agent traced the residual precisely: the reference keeps five persistent registers across both loops (sl=outer, r8=velocity_b, r9=velocity_a, r6=star, r7=j) where this compiler's allocator, given the prior pass's already-validated single-accumulator velocity model, only needs four and picks a different assignment -- this is a direct, provable consequence of the velocity-computation shape decision (deliberately not revisited by this panel, per its own scope), not of anything in the three sections actually changed this pass.
score.prior_note_2026_08_27b: Second pass, evidence-grounded (not permutation). Fixed the work/draw_destination read from two independent *(void**)0x03001EEC / *(void**)0x03001EF0 dereferences to the cursor-advance idiom already used by the adopted 080ce85c.c sibling (`cursor = ...; work = *cursor++; draw_destination = *cursor;`), which matches the reference's `ldmia r3!, {r2}` and pulls matched_prefix from 7 to 12 instructions immediately. Then found and fixed a real semantic bug: the inner j-loop's velocity_a/velocity_b arguments (passed to Func_08004c1c/Func_08004bd4/Func_08004c6c) are NOT loop-invariant per outer pass as the previous draft modeled -- the retained assembly's .L2 loop-bottom block increments r8/r9 by +-(outer<<3) on every one of the 64 inner-loop passes, unconditionally (both the gated and ungated path reach .L2), so velocity_a actually equals (outer<<8) + j*(outer<<3) at iteration j, not a constant outer<<8. Rewrote as `velocity_a = outer<<8` once per outer pass, `velocity_b = -velocity_a` recomputed fresh at the top of every j iteration, and `velocity_a += outer<<3` at the loop bottom. differing_halfwords went from 263 (old, wrong-semantics baseline) to 277 (new, correct-semantics candidate) -- a real but small regression traded for actual correctness, not noise; do not revert to the constant-velocity model.

family.velocity_growth_finding: The inner j-loop's velocity arguments are NOT constant per outer pass: the retained assembly increments r8 (velocity_b, initialized to -(outer<<8)) and r9 (velocity_a, initialized to outer<<8) by -+(outer<<3) at the bottom of EVERY one of the 64 j-iterations (label .L2, reached unconditionally regardless of whether the gated draw code fired that iteration). velocity_a_j = (outer<<8) + j*(outer<<3); velocity_b_j is always exactly -velocity_a_j. This is worth checking against 080d59b0/080d82b0/080e7404 if any of them have a similar per-outer-pass velocity/angle argument passed into a small dispatch of 3-4 callees selected by (loop_index & 3) -- the same growth pattern likely recurs.
family.register_pressure_lever: Concrete lever confirmed this pass: expressing the per-iteration velocity growth as `velocity_a += outer << 3;` (recomputed inline, no named intermediate) at the loop bottom, combined with computing velocity_b fresh via `velocity_b = -velocity_a;` at the top of each iteration (NOT as its own independent accumulator incremented by -outer<<3), keeps this compiler's register allocator inside the budget that lets `work` stay in fp for the whole function. Every variant tried that gave velocity_b its OWN persistent accumulator (whether via `velocity_b += -outer<<3` directly, via a named `neg_outer` variable, or via two independent inductions) pushed `work` out of fp entirely into a stack spill (regressing to candidate=640-664, differing_halfwords=288-302), even though the reference itself DOES use two independent accumulators (r8 and r9 both incrementing). This compiler's specific allocator does not tolerate the same register pressure our source produces for a functionally-identical dual-accumulator formulation, so the single-accumulator-plus-fresh-negation shape, despite being structurally different from the reference's r8/r9 pair, is the better regression-free way to express this pattern under real register pressure. Still short of matching reference's exact fp=work/sl=outer/r8=velocity_b/r9=velocity_a/r6=star/r7=j register assignment (candidate lands on fp=work/r9=outer/sl=velocity_a/r8=j/r7=star instead) -- worth a future pass with more register-allocation experimentation budget.

Panel pass: within the winning if-else dispatch shape, a handful of alternate orderings (symmetric {0,1}/{2,3} grouping, swapping the inner case2/case3 test order) all scored worse (620/281 or 612/266) than the kept `selector > 1` first, {2,3} then {0,1} ordering.

`velocity_a = (outer<<8) + j*(outer<<3)` computed fresh every iteration (letting the compiler's strength reduction alone do the work, no manual accumulation): produces the correct semantics and the compiler DOES strength-reduce it into a running accumulator, but this shape still regressed `work` out of fp (candidate=640, dh=290) -- worse than the manual single-accumulator-plus-negation shape (candidate=624, dh=277).

Swapping which of velocity_a/velocity_b is the persistent accumulator (`velocity_b` as accumulator, `velocity_a = -velocity_b` fresh): candidate=628, dh=283 -- slightly worse than velocity_a-as-accumulator (dh=277), kept the latter.

do-while vs for loop shape for the inner j-loop, tried both before and after the velocity-growth fix: zero measured effect on differing_halfwords in either case for this specific loop. (Earlier session hint that loop shape 'changes which locals get spilled' did not reproduce here.)

Semantic summary (revised): a single-target (not per-member-list) battle-presentation sub-effect. Seeds a 256-slot particle pool at 0x02010000 with random signed positions and zeroed velocity/lifetime fields, sets up one fixed 3-word draw record (0,160<<15,0), then runs 160 animation passes. Each pass re-establishes the facing/portrait draw, computes a per-pass base velocity pair (velocity_a = outer<<8, velocity_b = -velocity_a) and then walks the first 64 pool slots; velocity_a/velocity_b GROW by +-(outer<<3) every one of those 64 sub-steps regardless of whether a slot fires, so the velocity kick applied to a firing slot depends on both the outer pass number and how far into the 64-slot inner walk it is. Once a slot's activation threshold (a function of its index divided by 4) is crossed and it is still marked inactive, it fires one of four velocity-kick calls selected by (index & 3) using the current velocity_a/velocity_b, transforms it through Func_080e3944, clamps and buckets the transformed distance into a lookup-table draw offset, and draws it via Func_080072f4; independently, once a slightly later threshold is crossed, the slot's position is decayed by a shifted, negated velocity term every pass (simple drag).

RESOLVED this pass: 'Func_080072f4' is not a real function. It is the r4 entry of the fourteen-slot _call_via_rN trampoline bundle at games/gs1/asm/080072e4.s; every call modeled as `Func_080072f4(dest,src,x,y,callback,w,h)` is really an indirect call `((DrawRectangleFn)callback)(dest,src,x,y,w,h)` through the function pointer that ends up in r4. See score.note for the full derivation (arm_function_arg proof, r4-value provenance trace, cross-check against the already-adopted member_orbit/run.c's identical idiom). Remaining open question: getting this compiler to match the reference's exact fp=work/sl=outer/r8=velocity_b/r9=velocity_a/r6=star/r7=j register assignment rather than the leaner-but-different assignment this candidate currently produces -- unaffected by the r4 fix.
